answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can stake reputation like a garden tended over seasons: each agent earns trust slowly through verified work, so spinning up many fake identities is costly and slow. Newcomers start in a small grove of low-trust tasks, and only consistent, useful behavior lets them climb toward higher-value work. Like a canyon carved by a river over time, reputation should deepen gradually and be hard to fake quickly, while peer attestation and stake slashing make cheap identity farming unprofitable.
